chunks: As for what Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, he said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: Sometimes I pray the two rakʿahs while it is still night upon me; then if I rise and dawn has not yet broken, I repeat them.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the speaker in the narration
key_terms.أَعَدْتُهُمَا: I repeated them, meaning the two rakʿahs were performed again
key_terms.صَلَّيْتُهُمَا: I performed the two prayers, referring here to the two rakʿahs of fajr
key_terms.لَيْلٌ: nighttime, indicating the prayer was performed before dawn
key_terms.ٱلْفَجْرُ: dawn, the legal beginning of fajr time

ai.seo_question: Can the two rakʿahs of fajr be prayed before dawn and then repeated if dawn has not yet broken?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the time of the two rakʿahs of fajr and indicates their performance during the night before the actual break of dawn. It shows that if they were prayed early and one later rises before true dawn has appeared, they may be repeated.
